newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWF trims Australian barley crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWF trims Australian barley crop forecast.

text.p: Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd (AWF) trimmed its eighth forecast for Australia's 1996/97 (April/March) barley crop to 6.03 million tonnes from 6.14 million tonnes in its previous forecast a month ago.
The Australian barley harvest was now in progress and the crop was coming off very quickly, AWF said.
The Queensland crop had been yielding well and about 30 percent of the early deliveries were malting quality, it said.
The Queensland harvest was a little more than half completed, it said.
In New South Wales (NSW) there had been some frost damage to two areas of the northwest, it said.
This had produced low yields in the two areas, lightweight grain and a high percentage of screenings, it said.
Because the NSW crop had so far been free of substantial amounts of weather damaged wheat, domestic prices of feed quality barley firmed over the last week, it said.
There was a limited amount of black tip grain in the central west and northern Riverina. But there had been two weeks of fine weather and later maturing crops were of high quality, it said.
The long growing season in the south of the state was helping production of malting quality grain, it said.
There is a wide margin between the price of malting grade barley and feed barley, it noted.
In Victoria severe frost occurred when some of the eastern Mallee crops were flowering. The impact had been mostly on yields rather than grain quality, it said.
Victorian yields had been reduced because of this and dry weather in the first half of November, it said.
Only 10,000 tonnes of barley had been received into the Victorian grain handling system, it said.
At least 70 percent of the Victorian crop should be of malting quality, it said.
The South Australian crop had finished well and the harvest was in progress, it said.
The sudden end to the growing season removed some of the yield potential in the lower north and northern areas, it said.
AWF increased the area estimate for Western Audstralia (WA), producing an increase of 200,000 tonnes in forecast production for the state.
Late rain in the growing season for southern crops helped with grain size, it said.
